newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT -JGBs range-bound, looking for investors.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -JGBs range-bound, looking for investors.

text.p: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) are expected to be static and trapped within a relatively narrow range during Tokyo trading time on Tuesday amid a lack of fresh factors, traders said.
Although the market will watch to see how the Nikkei 225 responds to Monday's recovery in U.S. stocks, little impact is expected as the influence of stock moves has waned in recent days.
The big focus is likely to be on whether or not investors, sidelined recently by summer vacations, return to the market, and how they move if they do.
But even should investors decide to sell, traders said it was unlikely the key September 10-year bond would fall below 126.60, where bargain-hunting is expected.
One trust bank trader said he sees support initially at Monday's low of 126.84, and then at 126.73.

Gains are expected to be limited by concern about buying at the current high level as well as wariness about possible profit-taking sales should stocks show signs of falling. But traders said such sales are not expected unless the Nikkei slides to the lower end of 18,000, and are likely to be somewhat limited even then.
Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is expected to have virtually no impact amid a market consensus that there will be no change in U.S. interest rate policy.
